chapter: Kansas City, Basie, Prez and Booker Pittman
title: Booker T. Washington Hotel, Elnora's restaurant and Maceo Pinkard
summary: Hinton and Budd recall the Eblon, hotel, Street's and Elnora's restaurant, and Pinkard's drugstore.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Now they had built a place called the Booker T. Washington Hotel, right across from the Eblon Theater. You probably know that --
That Eblon was on the right, and Booker T. was on the --
That's right. I don't know if they changed the names, but --
(Inaudible) on the left, on the left.
Street's was around the corner, on the left. That's right.
And what's that name? That had the restaurant downstairs there? Her husband was a one-legged man.
Oh, oh, oh, oh, oh, oh. No, no, downstairs. That used to be known -- called the Subway. But it may have changed names since I was over there.
No, around the corner, on the corner there.
OH, the corner. Elnora.
Elnora, was its name.
Yeah, well we used to eat in there, get the most beautiful meals like for 25 cents.
That's right. I just wanted to bring
that up to sort of --
And -- yeah.
That I wanted you to know that -- and let the public know, that we're listening -- listening to us, that we're aware of the same territory.
Oh of course, you are so right, because like you know. I had forgotten that. How could I ever forget Elnora's Restaurant?
The little restaurant.
Oh, --
Her old man had one leg.
That's right.
Had a wooden leg.
What a beautiful person she was. All the musicians ate there.
Oh, yeah!
And at the time Maceo Pinkard had a drug store on the corner --
Yeah, right.
-- became Basie's business manager, and he gave up that drugstore to go out and take Basie's band, the first time you know, that Basie went on the road.
Right.
